conflicts.subject: note
conflicts.detail: Note primary keys differ (A: integer, B: uuid)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: uuid (text) primary key for Note and Tag in the unified app; A's integer ids kept in legacy_id during migration, B's uuids kept as-is

conflicts.subject: note-update-semantics
conflicts.detail: A's PUT sets only title and body; B's PUT merges the whole request body into the note (Object.assign), so a client can overwrite id, pinned or labels
solutions: Whitelist title and body on update; pin/unpin and tags through their own endpoints
conflicts.recommended: Whitelist title and body; reject unknown fields with 400

resolution.decision: Update whitelists title and body; unknown fields rejected with 400; pin/unpin and tags have their own endpoints

conflicts.subject: notes.list.order
conflicts.detail: Rule notes.list.order differs (A: "created_at desc", B: "pinned first (insertion order otherwise)")
solutions: Choose one value and record why
Make it a setting if both are legitimate
conflicts.recommended: Pick one value with the user; make it configurable only if both are needed

resolution.decision: One order everywhere: pinned first, then created_at descending (keeps A's order for unpinned notes, adds B's pinning); not configurable

conflicts.subject: jotter-data-in-memory
conflicts.detail: B keeps notes only in process memory, so there is no stored B data to migrate; any live B data can only be captured from a running instance before it stops
solutions: Treat B as having no data to migrate
Capture a running instance's GET /api/notes output (needs approval to run or call it)
conflicts.recommended: Plan the B import from a JSON dump of GET /api/notes; if none exists, B has no data to migrate

resolution.decision: B has no stored data; import only from a JSON dump of GET /api/notes if the user supplies one, otherwise nothing to migrate

conflicts.subject: labels-to-tags
conflicts.detail: B stores labels as a free-text array per note (duplicates allowed); the kept model is A's shared, uniquely named tags. Migrating labels collapses duplicates and case variants
solutions: Map each distinct trimmed, case-folded label to one tag and link it
conflicts.recommended: Map labels to tags (trim, case-fold, de-duplicate); log merged variants

resolution.decision: Map each distinct trimmed, case-folded label to one tag and link it; log merged variants

conflicts.subject: note
conflicts.detail: Note exists in A:Note, B:Note; fields not shared: created_at (only A), labels (only B), pinned (only B), updated_at (only B)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: Merge into one Note table: id, legacy_id, title, body (B content), pinned, created_at, updated_at; field origins listed in architecture.json

conflicts.subject: backend-runtime
conflicts.detail: Several runtimes: node: B; python: A
solutions: Choose one backend runtime and rebuild the features from the other
Keep two services only if a kept feature truly needs the other runtime
conflicts.recommended: One backend runtime for the unified app, chosen in the architecture phase

resolution.decision: One backend runtime: Python (A's runtime); B's features rebuilt in Python

conflicts.subject: export-filenames
conflicts.detail: B names export files <title>.md, so equal titles collide and titles with / or other unsafe characters produce bad paths
solutions: Slugify title and append a short id
conflicts.recommended: Slugify title plus first 8 characters of the uuid

resolution.decision: File name = slugified title + '-' + first 8 characters of the uuid + '.md'

conflicts.subject: fields
conflicts.detail: Field naming styles differ (camelCase: B; snake_case: A)
solutions: Pick one naming style for tables and fields and map the others
conflicts.recommended: Use one style (snake_case is usual for SQL)

resolution.decision: snake_case for all tables and fields; B's camelCase mapped (updatedAt -> updated_at)
